p10-l01.q: How many instructions does the subs/bne loop execute for N = 250 000?
In QEMU with -icount shift=0, how many SysTick ticks does that take (40 instructions per tick)?
On a Cortex-M3 at 72 MHz with 4 cycles per iteration, how many ms do 100 000 iterations take?
A taken branch costs 1 + P cycles. With P = 3, how many cycles is one loop iteration (subs 1 cycle)?
p10-l01.explain: The subs plus the branch with its refill.

p10-l01.q: Which register holds the return address after a BL (function call)?
What does QEMU’s -icount shift=0 let you measure exactly?
p10-l01.explain: Time advances 1 ns per instruction; there is no pipeline or wait-state model.

p10-l02.q: size reports text 1200, data 64, bss 256. How many bytes does the flash image take?
Static RAM for that build (data + bss), in bytes?
p10-l02.explain: Initialised and zeroed variables both live in RAM.

p10-l02.q: Reset_Handler is at 0x100. What value is stored in the reset vector (decimal)?
Initial SP for 128 KiB of RAM starting at 0x20000000, in decimal?
In nm output, what does U mean?
Why does the vector table need KEEP in the linker script?
p10-l02.explain: The hardware reads it, not your code.
options: nothing in the code references it, so --gc-sections would drop it

p10-l03.q: .text is 0x1F0 bytes at 0x0. What is the LMA of .data (decimal)?
.data is 8 bytes at 0x20000000 and .bss is 1024 bytes. Where does .bss end (decimal)?
With 64 KiB RAM, 4 KiB stack and .bss ending at 0x20000408, how many bytes of heap remain?
How much flash does .data with 200 bytes of initial values use?
p10-l03.explain: Its initial values are stored in flash (and it uses 200 bytes of RAM too).

p10-l03.q: What does ‘> RAM AT > FLASH’ mean for .data?
options: it is copied from RAM to flash at reset
it runs from RAM (VMA) but is stored in flash (LMA)
it is placed twice by the compiler

p10-l03.q: In C, how do you get the value of the linker symbol _estack?
p10-l03.explain: Linker symbols are addresses, not variables with storage.

p10-l04.q: Offset in the vector table of external interrupt IRQ 5 (decimal)?
Copying 4 KiB of .data at about 4 cycles per word on a 64 MHz core takes how many µs?
What does the core read from address 0x00000000 at reset?
p10-l04.explain: Word 0 is SP, word 1 is the reset vector.

p10-l04.q: Why does the test poison RAM with 0xA5 before checking .bss?
p10-l04.explain: Real RAM powers up with garbage; the test must too.
options: QEMU RAM starts at zero and would hide a missing .bss loop

p10-l05.q: Which MODER bit is the lower bit of pin 7’s field?
Value to write to BSRR to clear pin 3 (decimal)?
Address of GPIOC’s ODR (decimal), with ports 0x400 apart from GPIOA at 0x40020000?
Mask to clear the MODER field of pin 5 (decimal)?
Why use BSRR instead of ODR |= bit in the main loop?
options: a single store sets or clears pins atomically, so an interrupt cannot lose an update

p10-l05.q: You write to a GPIO register but nothing changes. The most common cause is…
options: the port’s clock is not enabled in RCC
the compiler optimised it away even with volatile

p10-l06.q: Result (decimal) of inserting 5 into that field of 0xFFFFFF0F?
How many (position, width) pairs are there for fields inside a 32-bit register?

options: it shifts a signed int into the sign bit, which is undefined behaviour
every access is performed, in order, and not cached in a register

p10-l07.q: HSE 8 MHz, M = 4, N = 168, P = 2. SYSCLK in MHz?
Flash wait states at 120 MHz (one per 30 MHz)?
With APB1 = HCLK/4 at 168 MHz, what clock does TIM2 see, in MHz?
p10-l07.explain: Timer clock doubles when the APB prescaler is not 1.

p10-l07.q: SysTick reload for a 1 kHz tick at 100 MHz?
When moving from 16 MHz to 168 MHz, when do you raise the flash wait states?
p10-l07.explain: Too few wait states for even a few cycles corrupts instruction fetches.
options: after switching SYSCLK to the PLL
before switching SYSCLK to the PLL
only if the ART accelerator is off

p10-l07.q: Which constraint rules out M = 2 with an 8 MHz crystal?
options: the VCO input would be 4 MHz, above the 2 MHz limit

p10-l08.q: f_clk = 84 MHz, PSC = 83, ARR = 999. Update frequency in Hz?
With PSC = 0, ARR = 1904 at 84 MHz, the update rate in Hz?
Frequency error of that setting against 44.1 kHz, in percent?
How long between wraps of a 16-bit counter at 1 MHz, in ms?
Why prefer PSC = 0, ARR = 4199 over PSC = 3, ARR = 1049 for 20 kHz PWM?
p10-l08.explain: The ARR range is the number of duty steps.

p10-l08.q: You wrote new PSC and ARR values but the old rate continues until the next wrap. Why?
options: PSC (and ARR with ARPE) are buffered until an update event; set EGR.UG to load now

p10-l09.q: SysTick reload for a 1 kHz tick at 25 MHz?
Cortex-M4 interrupt entry of 12 cycles at 168 MHz, in ns?
A 1 µs jitter budget at 168 MHz allows a critical section of at most how many cycles?
Measured periods range from 24 990 to 25 110 counts of 40 ns. Jitter in µs?
On a Cortex-M, which priority number is most urgent?
p10-l09.explain: 0 is the most urgent configurable priority.
The core goes straight to the next handler.
options: unstacking and restacking registers between back-to-back handlers

p10-l10.q: How many days until a 32-bit millisecond counter wraps?
A torn read of hi:lo at the wrap is wrong by how many ms?
p10-l10.explain: The new hi with the old lo.

p10-l10.q: A 4-cycle window at 168 MHz lasts how many ns?
flags |= bit compiles to load, or, store. How many hook positions (between accesses) let an ISR’s update be lost?
p10-l10.explain: After the load and before the store, in either of the two gaps.

p10-l10.q: Which of these is atomic on a Cortex-M3?
p10-l10.explain: Single aligned word accesses are atomic; compound statements are not.

options: if hi did not change across the read, lo was read while hi held that value

p10-l11.q: Centre-aligned PWM at 168 MHz with ARR = 4200. PWM frequency in kHz?
Edge-aligned with ARR = 999, CCR = 250. Duty in percent?
Dead time in ns for DTG = 0x94 at 168 MHz?
Largest dead time in µs with CKD = 0 at 168 MHz?

p10-l11.explain: Each output turns on late, after the other turned off.
options: every rising edge of CH1 and CH1N

p10-l11.q: Why is the counter peak in centre-aligned mode a good ADC trigger for current sensing?
options: it is the middle of a switching interval, away from the switching edges and their ringing

p10-l12.q: Counts per revolution of a 2500-line encoder in x4 mode?
1000 lines x4, 1 ms sampling, ΔN = 200. Speed in rpm?
Capture ticks (1 MHz) for one encoder cycle at 2 rpm with 1000 lines?
Which method is better at very low speed?
p10-l12.explain: Few counts per sample but long, well-resolved periods.

p10-l13.q: Conversion time in µs with 15-cycle sampling at 21 MHz?
Fastest trigger rate for a 4-channel scan with that timing, in kHz?
A 256-sample circular buffer at 4 channels and 10 kHz. Time between HT and TC interrupts, in ms?
Conversion time in µs with 480-cycle sampling at 21 MHz?
Why trigger the ADC from a timer instead of starting conversions in software?
options: the sample instants are as regular as the timer clock, with no software jitter

p10-l13.q: On a half-transfer interrupt, which part of the buffer should the CPU process?
options: the first half, while the DMA fills the second

p10-l14.q: Tuning word for 1 kHz at f_s = 100 kHz with a 32-bit accumulator?
Frequency resolution in µHz at f_s = 100 kHz?
Output frequency in Hz for M = 2^24 at f_s = 100 kHz?
Samples per cycle at 12.345 kHz with f_s = 100 kHz?

options: nothing special, it is the phase wrapping through 2π

p10-l14.q: Which bits of the accumulator index a 256-entry table?
p10-l14.explain: The most significant bits are the coarse phase.

p10-l15.q: IWDG timeout in ms with PR = 1, RL = 399 at 32 kHz?
The same setting at 47 kHz, in ms?
p10-l15.explain: The fastest LSI gives the shortest timeout.

p10-l15.q: Maximum IWDG timeout in seconds at 32 kHz (PR = 6, RL = 4095)?
WWDG tick in µs at 42 MHz with WDGTB = 3?

p10-l15.explain: The kick must prove the whole system is alive.
options: once per main loop, after every task has reported healthy

p10-l15.q: The window watchdog resets the chip if…
p10-l15.explain: The refresh must land in the window.
options: it is refreshed too late only
it is refreshed too early or too late
